successors.note: The Chera page does not say the Kalabhras took Kerala: it says 'between the third and fifth centuries CE' the Cheras 'saw a substantial decline in power', lists 'Disestablished c. 5th century CE' in the infobox, and says nothing about who held Kerala meanwhile. The successor link is a reading; Cliopatria has no Chera row after 305.

capitals.name: Muziris (Pattanam, near Kochi)

The page dates no capital; the years follow the shape (before the Kongu gain). Coordinates of Pattanam are standard geography, not from the page.

capitals.note: Infobox 'Vanchi-Karuvur (Karur), in the Kongu country'. The page dates no capital; the years begin with the Kongu gain of c. 180. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Karur.

keyframe_review.note: 25,200 km2 for -291..298 (central and southern Kerala, 76.0-77.4 E, 8.3-10.9 N, with the Palakkad gap but not Karur or Coimbatore). The page gives no area; it describes the territory as 'central Kerala and western Tamil Nadu (the Kongu country)'. Ok for -291..179: the page dates no territory before Chenguttuvan (c. 180), when it says 'Chera territory covered the Malabar Coast and the Kongu country'. The Mauryan empire never held Kerala (Maurya page: Kulke and Rothermund).

region.text: central Kerala, the Malabar Coast with Muziris

ledger.note: The Cheras exist by 291 BCE. Infobox 'Established c. 3rd century BCE'; the Cheras appear as 'Kedalaputo' in Ashoka's edicts, 'dated to the third century BCE'. The year -291 is Cliopatria's first shape, within the page's century. Reviewer (sa-02-a, 2026-10-19): confidence 1: the page gives only 'c. 3rd century BCE'; -291 is Cliopatria's year, as in the Chola and Pandya dossiers.

region.text: the Kongu country (Karur and Coimbatore), land that Cliopatria's Early Cholas shape holds and that the Chera page puts in 'Chera territory' under Chenguttuvan, c. 180 CE

ledger.note: c. 180: the Chera kingdom reaches Kongu. Chenguttuvan 'c. 180 CE' (the page says 'either the first or the last quarter of the second century CE'): 'Chera territory covered the Malabar Coast and the Kongu country'; the capital Vanchi-Karuvur (Karur) lies there. The page does not say the land was gained then, nor from whom: the counterpart is my reading, because Cliopatria holds Karur and Coimbatore in the Chola shape.

region.text: the Chera country at the end of the Sangam age

ledger.note: c. 305: the Early Cheras end in Cliopatria. The Chera page is silent: it gives 'between the third and fifth centuries CE' for a decline and 'c. 5th century CE' for the end. The Kalabhra page says they ruled 'sometime between the 3rd century and 6th century CE' (earliest inscription 270 CE) after 'the ancient dynasties of the early Cholas, the early Pandyas and Chera', and gives no date for the displacement.

certainty.note: No Chera frontier is recorded on the pages; the page describes territory only by regions (Malabar Coast, Kongu country, Palakkad Gap).

notes:
Group sa-02-a. Pages: Chera dynasty and Kalabhra dynasty (two, within the 1-2 page budget; the Chola dossier's Chola dynasty page is cited for nothing here).

THIN. The Chera page gives no area and dates no frontier. The two events with a page year are the Ashokan mention (founding century) and Chenguttuvan's territory (c. 180, dated by king). The founding and end years are Cliopatria's.

END DATE. The infobox says 'disestablished c. 5th century CE' and 'between the third and fifth centuries CE the Cheras saw a substantial decline in power'; Cliopatria ends the row in 305. A gap-filler should decide whether to extend the Chera shape (central Kerala and Kongu) to the fifth century; the page names no Kalabhra conquest of Kerala. No Chera row exists in Cliopatria between 305 and the Chera Perumals of Kerala (not in the table).

KONGU. The Chera page puts the capital Vanchi-Karuvur (Karur) in the Kongu country and the territory under Chenguttuvan (c. 180) across the Malabar Coast and Kongu; Cliopatria's Early Cholas hold Karur and Coimbatore throughout. The Chola dossier loses the land at 180 and this one gains it; delete both events and keyframes to revert to Cliopatria.

UNDATED, NOT ENTERED. Kings and wars named without dates on the page (Perum Cheralathan at Venni against Karikala; Chelva Kadumko Vali Athan 'c. 165 CE' defeating Pandya and Chola armies; Mantharam Cheral Irumporai captured by Nedunjeliyan II 'in the early 3rd century CE' and later regaining his territories) moved no border the page describes. Muziris trade dates (1st century CE) are not territory.

GAZETTEER. Kongu is described by Karur and Coimbatore radii; a 'Kongu' region entry would fit.
